title: Tutorial update: nanoparticle
body:
Convert the nanoparticle tutorial to the new-style example. Closes #1770 .

Also changed from "Exercise-solution" to "Annotated code" style of the tutorial, so that all code is complete and easier to test. 

# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [ ] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://ase-lib.org/development/contribute.html)

author: gelzinyte

comments.author: gelzinyte
comments.body: This sorts the html examples by the file name, not the length of the file. This gives us more control of how we want to order them, e.g. alphabetically or with a custom order by pre-fixing the file names with "XX_filename.py", as in this example.

comments.author: gelzinyte
comments.body: Not sure if it's ok to sneak it in here or if I should open a new issue or MR.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I guess we ideally want the same order as they have in the current documentation, since at least some of them are deliberately ordered (particularly the very first ones).  We could choose later if/when to change or deviate from that ordering.

Maybe the current ordering is arbitrary (is it really true that it sorts by the *length of the file*?) and then it doesn't hurt to set an ordering even if it's not the final one.

comments.author: gelzinyte
comments.body:
I agree, I think at least the "Introductory Examples" should have a bit of an order, starting with less complex examples. The [default ordering is by number of code lines](https://sphinx-gallery.github.io/stable/configuration.html#within-gallery-order) (not by length of the file..). This puts the nanoparticle example ahead of the other two, even though I think this is slightly more complex than the very first example should be. 

If we set the sorting to `FileNameSortKey`, then we can prefix the filenames with a number to enforce the order we want. There are other options, including providing your own sorting function, but I'm not convinced it's needed here. 

Please resolve the thread if you think `FileNameSortKey` is acceptable and can be included in this MR, or let me know what changes I can make.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Thanks for the explanation, it makes good sense.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Can we port the plotting code as we go along, so we use the OO interface instead of the "matlab" style one which is relies on changing global state?  Something like:

```
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.axvline(...)
ax.plot(...)
ax.set_xlabel(...)  # note minor name change
ax.set_ylabel(...)
ax.legend()
plt.show()  # this one is still somehow global but that's okay I guess
```

comments.author: gelzinyte
comments.body: Thanks for pointing this out, now updated.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Looks very nice with the plot and all.
